applies_why: The judge text enters an UNDERDETERMINED verdict for the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row on the ground that the competing readings leave neither chain forcing the other.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.
room: The phrase When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open: I weighed whether it forbids treating Acts 2:30's loins/seed wording as open and therefore UNDERDETERMINED when two readings are pressed, or whether it allows a tie between full chains despite the two-meaning verse.
why: By saying neither chain forces the other on the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row, the judge uses the single verse's two possible meanings as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 forbids because such a verse is not open and both meanings stand.
